topic: Clinic Missed-Call Recovery Map: 7 Safe Checks Before Automating Follow-Up
boundary: Educational operations guide only — not medical, legal, compliance, financial, marketing, revenue, savings, patient-growth, clinical, approval, or guaranteed-performance advice.

checks.owner_question: Which numbers, WhatsApp links, ads, reception lines and website buttons can create missed calls?
checks.safe_action: List each route before changing automation or scripts.

checks.owner_question: Which missed calls may need human judgment because they mention care, symptoms, complaints or sensitive data?
checks.safe_action: Use human review for sensitive or unclear items; do not let bots assess care needs.

checks.owner_question: What follow-up channel is appropriate: callback, WhatsApp, SMS, email or no message?
checks.safe_action: Use clear, minimal, non-diagnostic wording and respect opt-outs.

checks.owner_question: Who owns the first callback window, backup owner and escalation if reception is busy?
checks.safe_action: Create a visible owner rota before buying another tool.

checks.owner_question: Was the missed call caused by after-hours timing, busy staff, wrong number, ad mismatch, pricing query or appointment question?
checks.safe_action: Record a simple reason code so fixes target the real leak.

checks.owner_question: Could the note, recording, screenshot or bot transcript expose patient, customer or staff information?
checks.safe_action: Keep logs minimal, role-limited and free of unnecessary sensitive details.

checks.owner_question: Which repeat pattern should be fixed this week: staffing window, website CTA, ad promise, call routing or follow-up wording?
checks.safe_action: Improve one bottleneck at a time and label results as internal observations only.

safe_scope: Educational checklist for operational missed-call recovery; no medical, legal, compliance, financial, marketing, revenue, savings, patient-growth, clinical, approval or performance guarantees.
